To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamics of the propagation and decay of resonances is governed by the Kadanoff- Baym equation and that the self-energy of the propagating particle must be calculated consistently in a 2PI scheme.

the damping of the particles is a crucial ingredient of a transport description and that a systematic and general gradient expansion is available which is conserving and consistent with thermodynamics.

the dynamics of the resonance modes in nuclear matter is dominated by the damping of these modes, and that a transport description which properly accounts for the damping of the resonance modes can be obtained in a systematic manner by means of the Kadanoff Baym equation and the phi-derivation 2PI scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of resonances and their role in strongly interacting systems.
a consistent description of the dynamics and thermodynamics of strongly interacting systems in the presence of finite lifetimes of the particles.
the dynamics of resonances in nuclear matter and heavy-ion collisions.

this scheme is the best available approximation for the description of non-equilibrium dynamics of strongly interacting systems at finite densities and/or temperatures.
the 2PI method of Baym provides a very powerful tool for a consistent description of the dynamics and the thermodynamics of many body systems in the vicinity of equilibrium.
the 2PI scheme is a promising approach for transport descriptions of strongly interacting systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a systematic scheme for the construction of transport equations which properly account for damping widths of the particles in the medium.
the 2PI scheme is a promising tool for a consistent description of the dynamics in strongly interacting systems.

the 2PI scheme of Baym is a promising approach to describe the dynamics of strongly interacting systems in the regime of finite temperatures and/or densities, but that the present formulation of the gradient approximation for the transport coefficients has to be refined.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 2PI transport scheme provides a systematic framework for non-equilibrium transport descriptions of strongly interacting many-body systems which are based on a consistent and self-consistent description of spectral functions and their evolution.
the damping width of particles is an essential ingredient for a consistent treatment of the time-evolution in the non-equilibrium dynamics of strongly interacting systems.
the damping width of particles is not a simple phenomenological parameter but rather a consequence of the underlying dynamics.
